instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The attacking left-back of the side that led the title race by twelve points; genuinely good going forward, regularly exposed defending.
Thirty-one and losing his place; fifteen starts in his last regular top-flight season.
Thirty-three, thirty-seven starts, and a centre-half in a Bolton side that finished sixth; durable and well organised, never quick.
Thirty-five and a third-choice keeper covering three games; still competent, well short of the Newcastle regular of the mid-1990s.
Twenty-one league goals, but eleven of them penalties, for a side that went down. Genuinely explosive pace and a sharp finisher; limited in the air and in link play, so good rather than elite.
Seven starts across an injury-wrecked season; the pace that was the whole of his game had started to go with the knee.
Eighteen, and already the quickest player in the division; the end product was some way behind the pace.
His one season as a first-choice centre-half in a title-winning side; a good defender rather than the liability he is remembered as.
A centre-forward with genuinely elite touch and vision who dropped off the front to build play; the finishing was good rather than ruthless.
Twenty league goals and the Golden Boot; back to the level of his best Tottenham season.
Ten starts for a Leicester side relegated with 28 points; two seasons on from Derby and past his best.
Twenty-seven and reduced to ten starts by the knee and back problems that ended his career two years later.
A back injury ended his career at 28; five starts and no real football after them.
Five years and two divisions on from Newcastle; a promoted Fulham’s squad midfielder at 28, still a tidy passer and nothing more.
The last full season before the illness that ended his career at 31; still a competent Premier League centre-half here.
Ruptured cruciate ligament in the third game; he never played regular top-flight football again.
A season on from the cruciate rupture and visibly not the player of 1998/99; twelve starts, and then out of the top flight for good.
PFA Team of the Year in Wigan first top-flight season, and the best right-back in the division that year outside the top four.
Fifteen goals and eight assists at 22; strong, aggressive and a better footballer than the caricature. His peak season.
Twelve starts and six goals for a relegated Coventry before his knee gave out; the physical game was already blunted.
On loan from Lyon at 21 and visibly a good footballer for his size; rated as the raw version, not the Sevilla forward.
Eleven league goals from 27 starts; unusually mobile and technical for a forward of his size, and West Ham’s best attacker that season.
Higher at thirty-one than at twenty-six, which is unusual and here deliberate: he was a substantially better centre forward at Sevilla than in England, and African Footballer of the Year in between.
A record fee for a midfielder and an awkward first season positionally; the engine and the tackling were elite from the start.
Ten starts after a cruciate injury; the same player when fit, which is what the rating says.
Bolton’s best player at twenty-three: dominant in the air at both ends and already reading the game like a much older defender.
The right-sided supply line for the Quinn/Phillips partnership; the delivery was essentially the whole game.
Twenty-two goals for a promoted side that finished third; pace, power, finishing and genuine creation.
The decline from here is real and well documented — depression, loss of form, loss of the physical edge — rather than a run of bad luck.
Five starts, then retirement at 29; the athleticism and confidence that made him an 85 in 1995/96 were gone entirely.
A World Cup winner in a Chelsea side that conceded 30; rated at the Pallister anchor — good, occasionally elite, and error-prone.
Thirty-two, and a season away from Marseille; the passing was undimmed, the pace that covered for his risk-taking was not.
Thirty-three starts as first-choice centre-half in a Newcastle side that finished fourth; his best season.
Ten league goals from seventeen starts in his first Chelsea season; the touch and the link play were already the best parts of his game.
Twelve league goals in a title-winning side while spending much of the season dropping off the front to link play; a genuinely elite second striker.
Sixteen starts and two goals in a title-winning side built around Drogba; the link play was as good as ever, the goals were not his to score.
Thirty, on loan at Spurs after Barcelona and Monaco had each moved him on; a long way from the Chelsea forward of four years earlier.
Sixteen starts; a season broken up by an achilles problem, not a decline in ability.
Twenty-one league goals in his last United season; the finishing was untouched, and it was the relationship with the manager rather than the ability that ended it.
Thirty, and a back-up at Sunderland after relegation with Derby; four starts.
Thirty-five, three starts, and three seasons after his last regular top-flight football; a passing midfielder with nothing left physically.
Two seasons in Spain in between; back at City at 27 as a twelve-start squad forward, the awkward brilliance intact and the sharpness gone.
Ten goals and an England cap at twenty-four; the physical hold-up game finally had a finish attached to it.
Ten league goals from left-back, most of them penalties; a fearsome left foot and a genuinely hard defender, with obvious discipline and mobility limits.
The knee finally gave out; nine starts and retirement at 30.
Seven starts and one goal after a January arrival from River Plate; the struggle was settling, not ability.
Eight starts in a season interrupted by injury and a family bereavement.
Thirty, four goals, and a move to New York already agreed; the movement was intact but the sharpness in front of goal had gone.
